overview: We have all things again on the table right now, and we are working again I think the difference at this point is it's not an across the board, but it is no kidding One in which we work with the installations and their energy plans to ensure we're getting after what makes the most sense in that community Thank you, Assistant Secretary, and just for the record, there hasn't been any official directives issued or any other type of guidance issued related to renewable energy installations at our military bases as a degraded option or perhaps a non-option We have not issued an ORHIV I haven't given anything that would restrict us from taking the best opportunity to help our installations be energy resilient Thank you, Assistant Secretary, and to your point about things like battery storage We know that modern battery storage technology keeps getting better and better, hopefully more affordable as well And that technology could impact the overall reliability of things like closed grid solar systems What is your progress in identifying that technology, installing that technology, and having that storage on hand? I'm not trying to hurt anybody's feelings But it was 71 years ago we floated the first nuclear power vessel We were talking about three quarters of a century old technology And here we are 71 years later wondering how to power our bases America doesn't understand why we're not moving forward We built 219 nuclear power vessels for the United States military We have 6200 reactor years of incident-free operation I think when we discuss reliable, off-to-grid, independent, permanent energy for our military bases We have to, the Department of War, we have to be focused on small modular nuclear reactors But I digress because like everyone else up here, I want what I want from my state So, uh, Secretary Gillis, I said to Secretary Gillis Sportpoke and JRTC, the Joint Readiness Training Center Critical to Army Readiness, you concur? I do Absolutely So the Louisiana delegation has previously backed to 780 million in funding for military construction projects across the state Including more than 300 million for Ford Polk Yet we have a 5,000 bed deficit And we're housing service members and temporary substandard facilities At the same time, military construction projects, in some cases A carrying cross-premiums of 40 to 70% compared to the private sector So, Mr. Rogers, by virtue of almost every one of your bases having to be near water You experience stormwater challenges more so than almost anybody at that dais You know, I think I are experiencing, you said something very interesting and I'm going to quote you back We cannot Millcon our way out of this problem And that really resonated with me because right now, as we're addressing some of these very severe and very expensive Tens of millions of dollars of stormwater projects that are only going to get worse as C's rise We're struggling right now because it's competing with Millcon and ONM accounts And pushing back some other critical infrastructure projects on base And so I'm just curious because the GAO has identified gaps in the department's tracking of the full costs and operational impacts of natural disasters I'm curious, is there a different way we can look at this? Yes, private public partnerships are going to be a part of this But I think also the way that we're budgeting isn't necessarily keeping up with the new threats So has the department formally evaluated, evaluated, established a dedicated line of funding specifically for stormwater management And flood mitigation to proactively reduce long-term recovery costs and strengthen installation resilience? Yes, sir, absolutely Yes, come on Yes, thank you so much, I appreciate it gentlemen I've been proud to support the pilot program that created a Zillow type online real estate tool for the United States Army This has allowed the Army to see which buildings that we have deciding on Where it makes sense for new military construction And some of our installations, for instance on the historic Rock Island Arsenal We would be thrilled to welcome new tenants to even some of the historic and the newer buildings that are ready for tenants This tool has already likely saved the Army millions of dollars by averting the need for new building costs It's exactly the sort of smart common sense things that we've been able to do Things that we need to be doing Assistant Secretary Gillis, could you speak to the importance of this online real estate tool for the Army?
